{{Short description|Function in topology}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''quasi-topology''' on a set ''X'' is a function that associates to every [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] ''C'' a collection of mappings from ''C'' to ''X'' satisfying certain natural conditions. A set with a quasi-topology is called a '''quasitopological space'''.

They were introduced by Spanier, who showed that there is a natural quasi-topology on the space of continuous maps from one space to another.
